title: Horizon-aware prefix-slice scheduler and GPU-slab coordinator for mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a horizon-aware prefix-slice scheduler combined with a GPU-slab coordinator to reduce KV cache fragmentation and improve throughput/latency trade-offs on mixed prompt/response length workloads. The feature targets chat-style workloads with long prefixes interleaved with short responses (typical customer apps: conversational assistants, ticket summarizers).
background: We see significant GPU memory pressure and KV cache churn when serving mixed-length dialogs: long-context prompts pin large KV entries while short-turn responses produce many small allocations. Existing continuous-batcher heuristics favor aggregation but leave persistent fragmentation and high eviction churn under bursty traffic. Prior tickets focused on batching heuristics and KV eviction thresholds, but fragmentation and tail-latency regressions persist in realistic traffic (see ENG-331210, ENG-412005).
goals: Reduce KV cache eviction rate by >= 35% for mixed-turn workloads in staging traces
Improve 95th percentile latency under production-like bursts by >= 20% while keeping throughput +/- 5%
Avoid significant increase in average token cost (>5%) across benchmarks
Provide runtime flags to control horizon slice granularity and slab compaction aggressiveness
success_criteria: Staging load tests (Replay-A/B) show target KV eviction reduction and P95 latency improvements
Rollout experimentation shows no regression on customer-critical flows (conversational search test suite)
Operational metrics surfaced in Console (per-model KV eviction rate, slab fragmentation ratio, scheduler saturation)
implementation_plan: Design: define 'horizon' metric (expected remaining tokens based on request metadata + sampled generation distributions)
Scheduler: implement prefix-slice -> requests with long prefixes are split into a compact prefetch slice and a streaming slice; short responses are grouped into tight micro-batches
KV policy: introduce slab coordinator that allocates KV memory in variable-size slabs and coalesces small KV entries from short-turns into shared micro-slabs
Eviction: add horizon-weighted watermark (favor keeping high-horizon prefixes) and soft-locks for recently-prefetched slabs
Runtime flags: slice_size_ms, horizon_threshold, slab_compact_interval, micro_slab_target_size
Integration: expose metrics and tracing (KV residency time, slab occupancy, average slab fragment size) to Console
Testing: unit tests for slab allocator, simulated loadbench replay, staging A/B runs, canary rollout
experiments: Microbench A: vary slice_size_ms = [5, 10, 25] on a 16GB A100 cluster with mixed-turn synthetic workload; baseline continuous-batcher for comparison
Microbench B: compare slab sizes [32KB, 128KB, 512KB] and measure fragmentation ratio and average eviction churn
Production shadow: enable horizon-slice in shadow mode for 12h across two dedicated clusters and collect KV residency and P95 latency signals
Feature toggle A/B: roll to 10% traffic with slab_compact_interval=60s and measure cost per token and tail latency
tradeoffs: Smaller slices reduce KV pressure but increase scheduling overhead and potential for extra prefix recomputation
Aggressive slab compaction reduces fragmentation at the expense of occasional background CPU/GPU copies and transient latency spikes
Horizon estimation errors (overestimating remaining tokens) can cause unnecessary reservation and lower throughput
Tuning knobs increase operational surface area for customers using Dedicated/Private (we expose safe defaults)
risks: Incorrect horizon model could bias scheduling towards long requests and harm short-turn latency
Slab coalescing bugs could corrupt KV pointers under preemption/retry paths
Added complexity in allocator increases maintenance burden and risk of regressions in previously stable workloads
Telemetry gaps (missing per-slot residency) will make debugging hard without Console changes
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for slab allocator alignment, free-list correctness, and compaction invariants
Fuzzing: randomized slot allocation/release sequences to detect use-after-free in KV structures
Integration tests: end-to-end replay using realistic customer traces (anonymized), validating no token-loss and consistent outputs
Performance tests: long-running soak for 48h on staging with production-like burst patterns; measure eviction rates, GPU memory headroom, P50/P95/P99 latency
Chaos: simulate preemption of a worker GPU and validate safe slab eviction and recovery path
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow): 2 weeks shadow on staging clusters, collect metrics and tune defaults
Phase 1 (canary): 10% traffic on non-critical region with strict kill-switch metrics (KV_eviction_rate increase > 10% or P95 latency up > 15%)
Phase 2 (broader): 50% traffic with gradual increase to 100% if metrics stable for 72h
Phase 3 (opt-in): expose slab tuning flags to Dedicated customers as 'experimental' with docs and support runbook
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and console teams. Agreed on horizon definition and slab coordinator prototype. Action: Marco to sketch allocator API (PRD link added).
2026-02-20: Prototype allocator complete (bench-only). Observed 28% reduction in eviction on synthetic long-prefix traces when micro_slab_target_size=128KB.
2026-02-28: Scheduler prototype (prefix-slice insertion) integrated into continuous-batcher branch. Initial microbench shows P95 down 12% for mixed-turn set but throughput -3%.
2026-03-05: Discovered race under preemption in slab free path. Hotfix merged (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8321). Security review not required.
2026-03-10: Staging shadow run started for 48h. Early metrics: KV eviction -33%, slab fragmentation ratio reduced from 0.42 to 0.16, P95 latency improved 18% on target traces.
2026-03-12: Tuned horizon_threshold to 0.6 after false-positive reservations observed. Updated default slice_size_ms from 25 -> 10. Next: prepare canary config and runbook.
